indian.headline: Indian markets rose on realty and FMCG strength; US Fed rate hold provided steady backdrop.
indian.lead: Indian markets rose on realty and FMCG strength; US Fed rate hold provided steady backdrop.
indian.brief: Sensex climbed 1.24% and Nifty 50 gained 1.05% as real estate and consumer stocks led the charge.
why: Realty sector surged 2.8% and FMCG rallied 2.3%, lifting the broader market as domestic demand drivers outperformed.
US Federal Reserve held rates steady at 3.75%–4% on 28 October, removing immediate rate-hike fears and supporting risk appetite.
Elevated crude oil prices capped gains in energy stocks (+1.0%) and auto (−0.2%), offsetting some of the upside.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities ended a positive session on 29 October 2026 as realty and consumer stocks powered ahead. The Sensex rose 1.24% while Nifty 50 gained 1.05%, with Bank Nifty also climbing 1.18%. Real estate was the standout performer at +2.8%, followed by FMCG at +2.3%, signalling strong domestic demand. Individual stock moves added colour: Aeroflex Industries surged 14% on better Q2 earnings and 8-fold volume, while Paras Healthcare rose 5.4% after a modestly positive IPO debut, and Reliance Jio Platforms extended its post-IPO rally.

The broader market backdrop remained steady after the US Federal Reserve's 28 October decision to hold rates unchanged—a move that most analysts had priced in, so it provided reassurance rather than shock. However, crude oil's elevated levels weighed on energy and auto stocks, with energy flat at +1.0% and auto slipping 0.2%. Pharma and metals lagged, gaining just 0.6% and 0.7% respectively. The day underscored a domestic-demand-led rally with caution from global commodity pressures.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: US Fed holds rates; elevated oil tempers sentiment.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: Elevated prices cap energy and auto sector gains.

indian.watch: Track oil prices and Adani earnings momentum; realty and FMCG strength may sustain if domestic demand holds.

us.headline: US markets edged higher today as tech and financials led a broad but modest rally across all three major indexes.
us.lead: US markets edged higher today as tech and financials led a broad but modest rally across all three major indexes.
us.brief: S&P 500 gained 0.28%, Nasdaq rose 0.27%, and Dow added 0.19% in a positive session driven by strength in technology and financial sectors.
why: Tech sector outperformed with +0.8% gain, boosting Nasdaq and S&P 500 despite Microsoft's workforce cuts announcement offsetting profit growth of $36.6 billion.
Positive corporate earnings reports from Ford, Boeing, and Chipotle showed mixed but mostly profitable results, supporting investor confidence despite production delays and tariff concerns.
Financial sector gained +0.4%, suggesting steady banking and market sentiment despite broader economic headwinds including China's auto industry collapse and tariff threats to US-Canada trade.
us.narrative:
US stock markets finished in the green on October 29, with the S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow all posting modest gains. Technology was the clear winner, jumping 0.8%, while financials and energy each added 0.4% and healthcare rose 0.3%. The momentum reflects mixed corporate earnings—Microsoft reported $36.6 billion in profits despite announcing major layoffs, Chipotle shares surged 7% on sales growth signals, and automakers like Ford and Boeing posted results that beat or met expectations despite production headwinds.

Beyond Wall Street, market moves reflect growing global tensions and structural shifts. General Motors announced its historic shift from the New York Stock Exchange to Nasdaq on November 17, ending 115 years on the oldest exchange. Tariff threats loom large—Honda warned that 50% tariffs on Canadian auto parts would be catastrophic for the industry. Meanwhile, China's auto profits plummeted 22.8% in nine months, forcing Chinese carmakers to pursue overseas sales for survival. These structural forces—delisting moves, trade friction, and global supply chain stress—sit beneath today's otherwise calm market surface.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: CEO confidence on same-store sales growth through year-end boosted stock despite margin pressure.

tiles.label: Key data
tiles.sub: Strong earnings but tempered by announcement of major workforce reductions.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: Earnings strength offset by tariff threats, China slowdown, and production delays.

us.watch: Monitor GM's Nasdaq transition November 17 and watch for tariff policy updates affecting auto sector globally.
